idiom_name: tagged union of an inline char buffer and a {ptr, capacity} heap member (C11 anonymous unions)
implementation_notes: C has neither generic containers nor types with destructors, so the whole structure is written out: one union holding an inline buffer and a heap descriptor, a discriminator next to the length, and a small function family that hides which member is active. C11 anonymous unions help - cppreference notes that every member of an anonymous union is considered a member of the enclosing struct - and a union is only as big as its largest member, so the inline capacity is a compile-time constant the API must never expose. The spill path is one malloc plus memcpy plus the tag update, and release must test the tag before touching the pointer, because C cannot destroy a value for you; the invariants (tag matches the active member, length never exceeds the inline capacity in the inline state) remain the programmer's responsibility.
pitfalls: The union has no active-member tracking: reading buf after the tag switched to heap (or vice versa) is the classic bug - reading another member reinterprets the object representation and, since C99 TC3, the excess bytes are unspecified rather than defined, so update the tag at every write.

Alignment and padding: a union may gain trailing padding to satisfy its largest member, so sizeof(buf) is not always the usable inline capacity, and a non-char payload needs _Alignas (or a union with the payload type itself) before it can be placement-written.

Release is state-dependent: free(s->big.ptr) in the inline state frees an interior pointer, and forgetting to reset len/tag after a shrink leaves a hybrid object; keep allocation and release inside the same two functions that write the tag.
sources: cppreference, Union declaration (C) - anonymous unions are C11, a union is only as big as necessary to hold its largest member (plus trailing padding), and accessing a member other than the last written reinterprets the object representation: https://en.cppreference.com/w/c/language/union
